chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Yunus, from Husayn ibn al-Munthir, from Amr ibn Qays al-Masir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not leave anything that the community needs until the Day of Resurrection except that He revealed it in His Book and clarified it for His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and He made a limit for every thing, and He made a sign upon it that points to it, and He made a limit upon whoever exceeds the limit.

key_terms.حَدّاً: A limit, boundary, or prescribed penalty

ai.seo_question: What did Allah ensure was revealed for the community's needs until the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia doctrine of the comprehensiveness of divine revelation, asserting that Allah has provided explicit legal boundaries (hudud) and clear indicators for all essential matters required by the community until the Day of Judgment. It highlights the logical structure of divine law where every defined limit has a corresponding penalty for transgression, reinforcing the sufficiency of the Quran and Sunnah for legal derivation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Husayn Bin Al Munzar, from Amro Bin Qays Al Masir, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allahazwj Blessed and High did not leave anything out which the community would be needy for it up to the Day of Judgement, except that Heazwj has Revealed in in Hisazwj Book, and Clarified it for Hisazwj Rasoolsaww, and Made a Penalty (Hadd) for everything, and Made an evidence over it pointing towards it, and Made a Penalty (Hadd) to be upon everyone who exceeds the Penalty (Hadd)’.
